The technique is a key component of the Multi-Directional Sampling of Boundary Paths approach, enabling efficient sampling of boundary segments by decoupling them from the source and detector subpaths [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the technique involves sampling a boundary segment by first drawing it (via sampling a point on the evolving surface and a direction) and then constructing the source and detector subpaths. It further explains that this approach allows the contributions from the boundary segment, source subpath, and detector subpath to be 'decoupled' in the rewritten integral, thereby enabling efficient sampling without explicit silhouette search.
